findings.claim: APP_TABLE_HEIGHT now pins the table height the Playwright image renders with its fallback CJK font (560), so `pnpm test:e2e:layout` run the documented local way (host browsers via `playwright install --with-deps chromium`, testing.md:196) checks against a font environment it does not have.
findings.impact: A developer who runs the layout suite on an Ubuntu host set up as testing.md § Browser suites says gets the old runner's fonts and a table about 548px high. The test 'the app's own table is the height the claims are made about' (addon-policy.spec.ts:142-145) then fails, and so does the `wrapperHeight` check in 'the cap is 70% of the window' (:152). The failure is loud, not silent. The height was already environment-dependent before this commit, and only the environment it agrees with has changed. Spec §7 says local runs are unchanged.
findings.evidence: frontend/e2e-layout/addon-policy.spec.ts:27 `APP_TABLE_HEIGHT = 560`. :144 `expect(Math.round(m.tableHeight)).toBe(APP_TABLE_HEIGHT)`. decisions.md:13 says the image resolves system-ui and sans-serif to WenQuanYi Zen Hei and the fixture loads no web font. docs/developer-guide/testing.md:194-229 still tells developers to install host browsers and run `pnpm test:e2e:layout`, with no mention of the image.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (read-only). Expected: on an ubuntu-24.04 host after `playwright install --with-deps chromium`, `pnpm test:e2e:layout` reports tableHeight 548 against the expected 560.

bucket_proposal.reason: The revised I6 explicitly allows the 548→560 re-measure, and CI agrees with it, so no declared invariant breaks. What is missing is a statement that the layout constant is now tied to the image's fonts, which affects local runs.

findings.proposed_fix: Have testing.md § Browser suites say that the layout suite's measured heights are taken in mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.58.2-noble, or give the command that runs it in that image.

specification_compliance: Commit 78e058f2c changes only frontend/e2e-layout/addon-policy.spec.ts: APP_TABLE_HEIGHT goes from 548 to 560, and the comment's threshold changes from 783px to 800px. The revised I6 (r3) allows exactly this change, and decisions.md:10-14 records the human decision after CI run 44498253376.

The HEIGHTS table stays consistent under the new constant. The cap is 0.7·height and the assertion is `height*0.7 < 560`. 667→466.9, 715→500.5 and 745→521.5 are true (innerScroll true). 807→564.9 and 863→604.1 are false (innerScroll false). No declared innerScroll flips. The 807px case now sits 4.9px above the threshold, where it used to sit 16.9px above.
The new comment ('scrolls below an 800px viewport') is arithmetically correct: 560/0.7 = 800, and at exactly 800 the expression `560 < 560` is false.

The commit does not touch ci.yml, check-playwright-browsers.mjs or either new test. I re-read the working tree: the browser jobs (ci.yml:295-393) and the script (88 lines) match the reviewed diff. I1, I2, I3, I4 wiring, I5, I8 and I9 hold as in r1 and r2.

The fix list also contains commits merged from develop (pickup-coverage: addon submodule bump, useDiscover/useProviderShelfPage, watched-band.spec.ts). Those come from origin/develop through merge 0215ef84c and are not part of this change's diff against the base, so I did not review them as this change.
potential_unspecified_behavior: The layout suite's absolute table-height expectation now encodes the Playwright image's font resolution (WenQuanYi Zen Hei). The spec does not say which environment the layout constants are measured in, or that local host runs may disagree (CD-1).
regression_risks: The innerScroll=false case at 807px now clears the threshold by about 4.9px instead of about 16.9px. A future image font change of more than about 1% in table height would flip it. The failure would be loud.
A Playwright version bump that changes the image's font packages would move APP_TABLE_HEIGHT again. The browser check catches only the browser builds, not fonts.
test_coverage: addon-policy.spec.ts:142-145 asserts the measured table height equals APP_TABLE_HEIGHT, and :169 ties each HEIGHTS entry's innerScroll to the constant. A wrong re-measure would fail in CI, so the constant is self-checking in the image.
Mutation in thought: APP_TABLE_HEIGHT = 565 would fail :144 in the image (560 measured) and flip the 807px innerScroll expectation at :169. Both kill it.
Nothing checks that the documented local procedure reproduces the CI font environment.
not_verified: I ran nothing. Neither the layout suite nor the vitest and pytest tests were executed, and the table heights of 560 in the image and 548 on a host come from decisions.md, not my own measurement.
